name: brochure_zip
title: What everybody wants to know about the Empire State [electronic resource] : facts and figures --
credit: Empire State, Inc., [1931] (catalogued as [1930?]; text includes the 1 May 1931 opening). Columbia University Libraries, Durst Old York Library
license: Public domain (US): 1931 promotional brochure, no copyright notice on any page; Columbia University Libraries: "Digital version available with no restrictions"
used: p.2 statistics: red marker over 'Four and one-half stories of steel were erected every week' -> film 19.0-23.25 s; the '80 hours' sentence strip -> 25.25-28.0 s; the four scale outlines (Woolworth, Eiffel, Chrysler, Empire State) lifted off the page -> chart 35.5-43.25 s
p.3 map -> 5.0-8.75 s; heading 'THE MEN WHO DID THE JOB' (heading only) -> 28.0-29.5 s; chronology strip as the tower's footing -> 43.25-48.25 s

facts: 2,500 men a day / about 4,000 max, 4 1/2 stories a week, 80 hours, 1,250 ft / 102 stories, comparison heights, 17 Mar 1930 first steel, 15 Sep 1930 steel at 86th floor, 1 May 1931 opened nearly a month ahead of schedule (see FACTS.md)
